R0179.title: Industrial IoT (IIoT) Security Risks
R0179.definition: Special security threats faced by Industrial IoT devices and systems that may lead to production disruption, equipment damage, or personal safety accidents.
R0179.description: Industrial IoT connects critical infrastructure such as production equipment, sensors, and control systems. Attackers can infiltrate IIoT devices to: tamper with production parameters causing product quality issues, damage equipment operation leading to safety accidents, steal industrial secrets, launch targeted ransomware. IIoT devices typically have long lifecycles, are difficult to update, use insecure industrial protocols (such as Modbus, SCADA), and have expanded attack surfaces when interconnected with IT networks.
R0179.influence: Production line paralysis, equipment destruction, personnel casualties, industrial secret leakage, supply chain disruption.

observables: Industrial control systems (SCADA/PLC) show anomalous connections and commands originating from the IT network or the public internet
Production parameters are tampered with without authorization, causing product quality anomalies or equipment operation deviating from safe thresholds
IIoT devices use unauthenticated industrial protocols such as Modbus, with commands susceptible to man-in-the-middle tampering
After interconnection of the industrial control network with the IT network, the attack surface of OT devices expands, with scanning and probing behavior emerging
